item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports adaptive combinations of multiple interests and temporal scales. [FAME (WSDM 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01457) predicts separately from attention-head representations, combines their predictions through gating, and adds within-head experts for diverse preferences. [Mixture of Sequence (WWW 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20858) addresses interests that disappear and recur across sessions: theme-aware routing extracts coherent subsequences, then fuses global, short-term, and theme-specific experts. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) combines hypergraph session representations, contrastive intent clustering, Hawkes processes for repeated intent, and attention-based short-term adaptation. These suggest that older interactions can retain value when they match the current intent; uniform recency decay may discard useful history.\n\nFor this benchmark, a practical hypothesis is a small gated model combining SASRec’s final state, recent-window pooling, and several learned attention pools over the full history. Route using history representations and observed time gaps; compare learned decay against position-only weighting. This is an implementation inference, not a demonstrated benchmark improvement. [HM4SR (WWW 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14269) provides precedent for explicit timestamp-conditioned experts, although its multimodal inputs and category supervision exceed the available contract. Complement/substitute semantics require caution: [TPNE (SIGIR 2023)](https://opus.lib.uts.edu.au/bitstream/10453/170069/2/SIGIR_23_TPNE.pdf) uses Amazon “also buy”/“also view” relations, unavailable here. History-derived transition experts can learn different temporal patterns, but should remain latent patterns rather than asserted complement or replacement labels. Select architecture and decay through the common macro validation HR@10."}
